messages:
olivia: heads up — seeing a spike across streaming endpoints, p95 ~650ms -> 2.1s, p99 ~1.2s -> 3.8s. first noticed at ~08:14 UTC after the prefixhash-v3 rollout. cache hit rate dropped from ~92% to ~11%.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3465 — latency SLO breach (streaming + gen). Paging oncall.

oncall-bot: Paging @raj (oncall). 08:15 UTC — SLO breach (p99 > 1s).

raj: I'm on it. dashboards show sudden surge in cache-miss rate for prefixcache.* buckets, and a lot of 'no-kv' tails in the streaming logs.

sam: support feed: 9 customers reporting timeouts, 3 stream disconnects with reconnect loops. CS is preparing an escrow message.

maria: can we confirm rollout target set? if prefix hashing changed keys we might have invalidated warm caches. suggest immediate traffic rollback for the rollout group and enable legacy-routing fallback.

olivia: checked rollout console — prefixhash-v3 targeted 30% across prod, currently at 28%. I can pull it to 0% now. plan: 1) pause rollout 2) route traffic off cohort 3) kick off cache-warmup for affected prefixes 4) monitor p95/p99.

raj: do the pause + force rollback. also enable bypass caching for streaming tail so requests hit model directly for a short window (to avoid stall recovery patterns).

olivia: running rollback command now:
```bash
# stop rollout and revert to v2 keys
curl -X POST \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  https://console.redwood.ai/api/rollouts/rollback \
  -d '{"rollout_id":"prefixhash-v3","target_percent":0}'
```

olivia: rollback submitted at 08:18 UTC. console shows target_percent=0.

kevin: starting cache warmup job for the affected prefixes. will run in 5m batches to avoid burst. job: `/ops/warm_prefix_cache --source=recent-traffic --batch-size=5k`

maria: also flip in-memory fallback for prefixcache so stale key hits return fallback payload (less ideal but prevents stalls). patch: `enable_prefix_fallback=true` in runtime config.

raj: query I ran: `SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95), percentile(latency_ms,99) FROM streaming WHERE env='prod' AND ts>now()-15m GROUP BY shard` shows p99 across shards trending down where rollout traffic reduced.

sam: CS note: we already contacted top-affected customers, asked them to retry, offering a postmortem once we stabilize. keeping product impacts to minimal, but one big enterprise (acme-inc) saw 10% failure rate on early morning batch jobs.

olivia: monitoring: cache-hit-rate for prefixcache main cluster at 08:16 = 11%, at 08:28 = 46% after rollback kicked off, p99 at 08:28 = ~700ms.

incident-bot: Update INC-2026-3465: rollback executed, warmup started, oncall assigned: raj -> handing to maria for mitigation + postmortem.

maria: taking over the incident. immediate next steps: 1) keep warmup job running 2) watch for client reconnect storms 3) schedule canary re-rollout only after 48h with telemetry gated tests (prefix-hit, p95, p99).

kevin: warmup logs: `warmed 48k keys in 20m` — we saw hit-rate jump to 84% by 08:42 UTC on main cluster. no error spikes in warmup job.

raj: observed streaming tail stalls clearing up as clients reconnect; p99 trending toward baseline (180-220ms) in most shards. leaving an eye on two small edge regions where TTLs were longer.

sam: capturing customer impact numbers for SLA reports: 12 total customers affected, 3 with reconnects, 1 enterprise with measurable job failures. will coordinate credits with finance/product after postmortem.

maria: handoff note for postmortem: root cause hypothesis = key-space shift from prefixhash-v3 salted keys + rollout mixing with v2 leading to cache namespace split and massive cold-read fanout. action items:
- revert rollout (done)
- add rollout-gate check for cache-hit delta > 20% in 10m window
- create automated warmup job triggered on rollout when key fingerprint changes
- add metric alert for prefix-hit-rate delta and streaming-tail-stall count

olivia: adding runbook steps to triage doc and tagging eng-runtime + eng-sre. will attach logs and queries in the postmortem doc.

maria: leaving handoff: monitor for 2 more hours, keep warmup running, no re-rollout until explicit approvals. I'll own the postmortem draft.

olivia: thanks — marking the incident as mitigated at 08:45 UTC. moving to monitoring state. follow-ups for postmortem + alerts assigned. :thumbsup:
